about: bank 1 $D6CD-$EA02: the 3-D object tables and the object routines carried from Star Wars' WSOBJ (load, perspect and draw an object), a set of unused threaded draw primitives, the high score display, entry and NVRAM copy, and the explosion queue (WSXPLD). also the names of the 22 object draw routines at $AD68-$D6CC

B1:AD68.name: draw_tie
B1:AD68.desc: draw routine of object 0, the TIE fighter of Star Wars (53 points, 88 lines at full brightness, points 1 to 51). like all 22 draw routines it is entered from obj_draw with A, B, X and U stacked, sets the direct page to the point buffer BJ_PNT, writes one vector per line into the display list at Y - the first one a blank move from the beam position BJ_CX, BJ_CY - then restores the direct page, leaves the last point in BJ_CX, BJ_CY and returns to obj_draw's caller

B1:B423.name: draw_tie_wing
B1:B423.desc: draw routine of objects 1 and 2, the left and the right wing with strut of an exploded TIE fighter (Star Wars' TDS_TI1 and TDS_TI2, explosion piece types 9 and 10): 30 lines at full brightness between points 1 to 18. the two objects differ only in their point tables

B1:B69A.name: draw_tie_cabin
B1:B69A.desc: draw routine of object 3, the centre cabin of an exploded TIE fighter (Star Wars' TDS_TI3, explosion piece type 11): 46 lines at full brightness between points 1 to 28

B1:BA37.name: draw_probot_body
B1:BA37.desc: draw routine of objects 4 and 5, which make one picture, the body of a probot: object 4 (19 points, a three-ring hexagonal body below the head) is perspected into buffer points 1 to 19 and object 5 (a hexagon of 6 points) into points 20 to 25, and this routine draws 36 lines, the last six from the body's top ring to the points of object 5. brightness of each line comes from the depth cue flags of its two points. page 2 processes object 4, then object 5 raised by the probot's bob offset, and draws once

B1:BDF1.name: draw_probot_head
B1:BDF1.desc: draw routine of object 6, the head of a probot (20 points, a flat dome of three hexagonal rings, 27 lines with depth cue brightness). the explosion code also draws object 6 for the pieces of a destroyed probot (piece types 0 to 2)

B1:C081.name: draw_probot_eye
B1:C081.desc: draw routine of object 7, which has the same point table as object 6: four lines round points 6, 13, 12 and 17 of the head, a four-sided figure on its front. page 2 draws it from the points perspected for object 6 after the head, in the colour its launch test chose

B1:C0FC.name: draw_limb_down
B1:C0FC.desc: draw routine of objects 9 and 11 to 16 in the table, used by page 2 for all eight probot limbs (objects 9 to 16, four points each, hanging below the body): writes colour instruction $6260, moves to point 0 and draws points 0-1-2-3 at full brightness

B1:C15C.name: draw_limb_up
B1:C15C.desc: draw routine of object 10: draws from the beam position to point 2, then to 1 and to 0, three lines at full brightness with no move first. page 2 calls it as object 10 after draw_limb_down for every limb with BJ_CX shifted, so the limb is drawn down one side and back up the other

B1:C1A4.name: draw_hexagon
B1:C1A4.desc: draw routine of object 8, a flat hexagon of six points (radius 60), six lines with depth cue brightness. page 3 draws it for the probot transmissions

B1:C247.name: draw_atst_head
B1:C247.desc: draw routine of object 17, the head (cab) of an AT-ST walker: 18 lines with depth cue brightness between points 0 to 13 of its 18 points

B1:C430.name: draw_atst_port
B1:C430.desc: draw routine of object 18, which has the same point table as object 17: four lines round points 12, 13, 15 and 14, the panel on the front of the AT-ST head. page 1 draws it from the points perspected for object 17, in the colour its aim test left

B1:C4AB.name: draw_atst_leg
B1:C4AB.desc: draw routine of object 19, one AT-ST leg: 33 lines at full brightness between 18 buffer points. the object's own table holds a single point, the 18 points are put into the buffer one at a time by page 1 through pnt_add_scratch

B1:C752.name: draw_atst_side
B1:C752.desc: draw routine of objects 20 and 22, the left and the right half of the AT-ST head as separate 8 point pieces, 11 lines at full brightness. they are the pictures of explosion piece types 3 and 5

B1:C840.name: draw_atst_top
B1:C840.desc: draw routine of object 21, a 6 point wedge made of the top and front points of the AT-ST head, 9 lines at full brightness. it is the picture of explosion piece type 4

B1:C91C.name: draw_atat_body
B1:C91C.desc: draw routine of object 23, the body of an AT-AT walker (24 points perspected into buffer points 1 to 24): 26 lines at full brightness between points 1 to 16

B1:CB40.name: draw_atat_neck
B1:CB40.desc: draw routine of object 26, which has the point table of the AT-AT head: four lines at full brightness from buffer points 17 to 20, which belong to the body (object 23), to points 22 to 25, the back of the head - the neck. page 0 draws it only when the body is in view

B1:CBE3.name: draw_atat_head
B1:CBE3.desc: draw routine of object 24, the head of an AT-AT (21 points perspected into buffer points 22 to 42, after the body's): 21 lines with depth cue brightness

B1:CE19.name: draw_atat_eye
B1:CE19.desc: draw routine of object 25, which has the point table of the AT-AT head: four lines round buffer points 38 to 41, the rectangle on the front of the head that page 0 turns red and tests the lazar against (the eye the player is told to shoot)

B1:CE94.name: draw_atat_leg
B1:CE94.desc: draw routine of object 27, one AT-AT leg: 18 lines at full brightness between 12 buffer points, three points at each of four levels joined into a three-sided tube. the object's own table holds a single point, the 12 points are put into the buffer one at a time by page 0 through pnt_add_scratch

B1:D005.name: draw_atat_piece
B1:D005.desc: draw routine of objects 28, 29 and 30, the front, middle and rear third of the AT-AT body as separate 8 point boxes, 12 lines at full brightness. they are the pictures of explosion piece types 6 to 8

B1:D123.name: draw_dart
B1:D123.desc: draw routine of object 31 (9 points perspected into buffer points 1 to 9): a long square shaft that widens to the rear, with a pointed nose. 18 lines at full brightness in three colours, written by the routine itself: $6180 for the nose, $6680 for the shaft and a JSRL $A013 before the rear end. page 0 loads it in the walker part's setup and draws it twice from the tow cable code (P0_972B on), what the two darts stand for I could not tell from here

B1:D2D3.name: draw_asteroid
B1:D2D3.desc: draw routine of objects 32, 33 and 34, one 24 point solid - a cube with every corner and edge cut off - in three sizes (1000, 500 and 250 units): 48 lines with depth cue brightness. page 2 loads all three for the asteroid field and draws object 33

B1:D84E.name: obj_list_init
B1:D84E.desc: entry of JINOBJ through the cross-bank table (bank 0 L60A2, called by init_general): saves X, runs JINOBJ below, which in ESB ends by pulling X and returning

B1:D868.name: obj_load_b
B1:D868.desc: loads object B into the math RAM: stores B in BJ_ID and runs obj_load. called through bank 0 L60A8 by the setup routines of the game parts, once for every object the part draws

B1:D86A.name: obj_load
B1:D86A.desc: Star Wars' JADOBJ, changed: copies the points of object BJ_ID from its ROM table (6 bytes each, address from obj_points_tab) into the math RAM at BJ_RAM (8 bytes each) and notes the block index in BJBIC, unless the object is already there. ESB rounds the point count up to an even number, keeps the counter on the stack, saves A, X and U, and returns without loading when the block index would overflow, where Star Wars had a SWI

B1:D8AC.name: obj_beam_home
B1:D8AC.desc: ends an object: sets the beam position the draw routines work from to the screen centre (BJ_CX = 0, BJ_CY = $68, which is minus VGOFFY) and adds a JSRL to vector ROM $32AC, the default scale and a centre instruction. called after every object draw and by bank 0 when a display list is started

B1:D92F.name: obj_points
B1:D92F.desc: perspects the points of object BJ_ID into the point buffer, ESB's version of JOBJPNT. the buffer address comes from obj_buf_tab, the depth cue range (plus the centre's distance M_XT) and scale from obj_cue_depth and obj_cue_scale go to M_XPS and M_YPS, and the math box programs $32 and $36, which Star Wars' microcode does not have, do the transform, the perspective and the depth cue of each point while the divider supplies 1/depth. each point is stored as screen x (limited to -534..534), screen y (limited to -532..728) and a flag byte with the top three bits of the cue, the intensity bits of a vector. the word at COLOR is left pointing past the last point. returns at once if the object is not loaded

B1:D9EF.name: pnt_buf_reset
B1:D9EF.desc: starts a new point list: the word at COLOR, the next free point of the buffer, is set to BJ_PNT ($4E00). called by pages 0 and 1 before they build the points of a walker leg

B1:D9F6.name: pnt_add_scratch
B1:D9F6.desc: perspects the single point in the scratch block M_X0 (block index $0F) with MS_PAD, the divider and MS_PERS, as Star Wars' JOBJPNT did for every point, stores its screen x and y at the buffer position in the word at COLOR and moves that word on by 5. the flag byte is not written. pages 0 and 1 call it for every joint point of a walker leg, which is then drawn as object 27 or 19

B1:DA2A.name: obj_draw_b
B1:DA2A.desc: draws object B from the points now in the buffer: stores B in BJ_ID and runs obj_draw. used to draw with another object's lines than the one whose points were perspected

B1:DA2C.name: obj_draw
B1:DA2C.desc: draws object BJ_ID: stacks A, B, X and U and jumps to the object's draw routine from obj_draw_tab, which unstacks them and returns to the caller. it replaces Star Wars' JOBJDRW, which interpreted a line list

B1:DA38.name: thr_start
B1:DA38.desc: unused code that the listing shows as data ($DA38-$DAB2): a threaded interpreter that draws the same vectors as the generated draw routines from a list. entered with X at a 3-byte instruction (a JMP here, where obj_draw's JMP ,X would have arrived) that is followed by 4-byte cells, each the address of a primitive and an operand. it points U at BJ_CX as the last point, steps X over the 3 bytes and jumps through the first cell. every primitive ends by stepping X to the next cell and jumping through it. no word in either bank, the slapstic pages or the vector ROM holds the address of any of the six entries, so nothing runs it

B1:DA3F.name: thr_move
B1:DA3F.desc: threaded primitive (unused): the operand is the address of a buffer point. writes a blank vector from the last point at U to it (y difference, then x difference, both masked to 13 bits), makes it the last point and goes to the next cell. it keeps the list pointer in the two stack bytes that hold obj_draw's saved A and B

B1:DA5D.name: thr_draw
B1:DA5D.desc: threaded primitive (unused): as thr_move, but the vector is drawn at full brightness (ORA #$E0)

B1:DA7B.name: thr_draw_cued
B1:DA7B.desc: threaded primitive (unused): as thr_move, but the vector's intensity bits are the sum of the flag bytes of the new point and of the last point, the depth cue that obj_points leaves

B1:DA9D.name: thr_word
B1:DA9D.desc: threaded primitive (unused): writes the operand word to the display list as it is, a colour instruction for example, and goes to the next cell

B1:DAA5.name: thr_end
B1:DAA5.desc: threaded primitive (unused), the end of a list: copies the last point at U to BJ_CX and BJ_CY and its flag byte to $48BE, then unstacks A, B, X, U and returns as the generated draw routines do

B1:DEE2.name: hs_view
B1:DEE2.desc: Star Wars' VWHSCR, changed: draws the high score table. with UPDFLG plus (initials being entered) it shows message $32 in the middle of the screen, rows from the half-screen table hs_ypos_half and, after the rows, the alphabet with RUB and END and the cursor. otherwise message $33 at the top, a larger scale and the full-screen rows THSY2. both messages have the legend JEDI KNIGHT, next to which the mark at vector ROM $326A is drawn. ten of the 25 entries are shown, from entry hs_scroll (held to 0-15): each row is the three initials (the one being entered flashes), the mark again if bit 7 of the first initial is set, the rank number and the 8 digit score. when no initials are being entered the yoke scrolls the table: cursor y beyond +-$140 steps hs_scroll by one every third frame

B1:E209.name: hs_rank_step
B1:E209.desc: called once a frame from bank 0 (L6303) through L60FC: when the player's score has reached the score of table entry rank_index (higher top word, or equal top word and the low word not below), rank_index is stepped down to the next better entry. does nothing once rank_index is minus

B1:E22D.name: hs_insert
B1:E22D.desc: Star Wars' UPDATE and PUTHI in one, for the 25 entry table of 7 byte records (3 initials, 4 BCD score bytes) at INITLS: finds the first entry the score S_SC87, S_SC43 is not below, moves the entries from there down by one (the last drops out), and writes the new one with the score and the initials in last_inits. UPDFLG = the entry's address, UPDINT = 0 and INITL = its first initial, or UPDFLG = $FFFF if the score is below all 25. hs_scroll is left at the entry's index less 5 so that the display shows it

B1:E363.name: jedi_mark_set
B1:E363.desc: tail of GETINT, also called before it moves to the next initial: if jedi_done is set and the first initial is the current one (UPDINT = 0), sets bit 7 of the initial at U. the display shows the Jedi mark beside entries whose first initial has that bit

B1:E3E8.name: hs_load
B1:E3E8.desc: start-up: fills the 25 entries with the defaults (hs_set_defaults), has NVRAM area 1 read and checked (K768E), copies the top ten entries (70 bytes) from the NVRAM image at nv_hiscores to INITLS and falls into hs_validate. Star Wars' SETINT

B1:E400.name: hs_validate
B1:E400.desc: Star Wars' CHKHIS for the 7 byte entries: checks every entry up to the end of the table ($4BEE) - three initials below $1B (bit 7 of the first ignored) and four score bytes that are BCD. on any bad byte it goes to DOINTS, which puts in the defaults and writes the top ten back to the NVRAM image. also called from bank 0 through L6114

B1:E458.name: hs_save
B1:E458.desc: copies the top ten entries (70 bytes from INITLS) to the NVRAM image at nv_hiscores and calls EECKSM for area 1. called when a player ends the entry of initials and by DOINTS

B1:E46D.name: hs_set_defaults
B1:E46D.desc: copies the 175 bytes of the default table hs_defaults, 25 entries, to INITLS

B1:E47D.name: hs_nv_defaults
B1:E47D.desc: copies the first 70 bytes of hs_defaults, the top ten entries, to the NVRAM image at nv_hiscores. called by the NVRAM code at K751E and offered to bank 0 as L611A, which nothing calls

B1:E53D.name: expl_clear
B1:E53D.desc: clears the timer byte XPS_TMR of every entry of the explosion queue XPQUE, so that no explosion piece is live. called through bank 0 L6186 by the setup of each part of a wave

B1:E57C.name: tie_expl_begin
B1:E57C.desc: cross-bank entry (L618C, called by page 3) that starts the explosion of the TIE fighter whose record is at X: clears byte 3 of the record and calls BGAXP with X and U saved. Star Wars' BGAXPLD without the CPUGON call

B1:E587.name: atat_expl_begin
B1:E587.desc: cross-bank entry (L6192, called by page 0) that starts the explosion of an AT-AT: BGTWXP with X and U saved. the centre is in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT

B1:E58E.name: probot_expl_begin
B1:E58E.desc: cross-bank entry (L6198, called by page 2) that starts the explosion of a probot: BGBKXP with X and U saved. the centre is in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT

B1:E595.name: atst_expl_begin
B1:E595.desc: cross-bank entry (L61A4, called by page 1) that starts the explosion of an AT-ST: atst_expl_setup with X and U saved. the centre is in M_XT, M_YT, M_ZT

B1:E59C.name: expl_stub_rts
B1:E59C.desc: a lone RTS that the cross-bank table offers to bank 0 as L619E. nothing calls it

B1:E718.name: atst_expl_setup
B1:E718.desc: begins the explosion of an AT-ST: piece types 3, 4 and 5 and an upward speed byte of 3 into TMPTP1, TMPTP2, TMPTP3 and TMPVZ, then the three-piece code it shares with BGTWXP at $E72E

B1:E87C.name: expl_piece_kill
B1:E87C.desc: move routine of explosion piece type 1 in TMV: clears the piece's timer, which ends it. no code here makes a piece of type 1

B1:E96C.name: vwx_probot_0
B1:E96C.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 0 (table expl_view_tab): object 6, the probot head, through VWTIN

B1:E970.name: vwx_probot_1
B1:E970.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 1: object 6 through VWTIN

B1:E974.name: vwx_probot_2
B1:E974.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 2: object 6 through VWTIN

B1:E978.name: vwx_atst_0
B1:E978.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 3: object $14 (20), one half of the AT-ST head, through VWTIN

B1:E97C.name: vwx_atst_1
B1:E97C.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 4: object $15 (21), the top wedge of the AT-ST head, through VWTIN

B1:E980.name: vwx_atst_2
B1:E980.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 5: object $16 (22), the other half of the AT-ST head, through VWTIN

B1:E984.name: vwx_atat_0
B1:E984.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 6: object $1C (28), the front third of the AT-AT body, through VWTIN

B1:E988.name: vwx_atat_1
B1:E988.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 7: object $1D (29), the middle third of the AT-AT body, through VWTIN

B1:E98C.name: vwx_atat_2
B1:E98C.desc: view routine of explosion piece type 8: object $1E (30), the rear third of the AT-AT body, through VWTIN

4C70.name: hs_scroll
4C70.desc: high score display: index of the first of the ten entries shown, held to 0-15 by hs_view. hs_insert leaves the new entry's index less 5 here, and while no initials are entered the yoke steps it up and down

4C71.name: hs_row_end
4C71.desc: high score display: hs_scroll + 10, the entry index at which hs_view stops

4C76.name: last_inits
4C76.desc: 3 bytes ($4C76-$4C78): the initials of the last high score entry made, saved when END is chosen (the first without its Jedi bit) and written into the next new entry as the initials offered

4C79.name: hs_scr_delay
4C79.desc: high score display: frames until the yoke may scroll the table again. set to 1 after a step, counted down to minus

4D04.name: nv_hiscores
4D04.desc: 70 bytes of the NVRAM image ($4D04-$4D49): the top ten high score entries, 3 initials and 4 BCD score bytes each, copied to and from INITLS

5075.name: m_zps_lo
5075.desc: low byte of M_ZPS: math box programs $32 and $36 leave a point's depth cue in M_ZPS, (M_XPS - depth) * M_YPS, and obj_points takes the top three bits of this byte as the point's intensity flag

ram_notes.COLOR: in the game the word at this address is the next free point of the perspected point buffer BJ_PNT: obj_points sets it to the object's buffer address and leaves it past the last point, pnt_buf_reset sets it to $4E00 and pnt_add_scratch stores a point there and adds 5

esb_notes.B1:D92D: only the entry is the same. obj_points below does not use MS_PAD and MS_PERS point by point: programs $32 and $36 of ESB's own microcode do each point, the points are 5 bytes with a depth cue flag, and they go to the buffer address of obj_buf_tab
esb_notes.B1:E29B: the fire or thumb switch edge picks a letter. RUB and a letter send sound commands $3B and $3F. END copies the entry's initials to last_inits, saves the top ten to the NVRAM image (hs_save), sends sound $38 and sets UPDFLG to $FFFF. after a letter the next initial offered is the one already in the entry. the routine ends in jedi_mark_set, which sets bit 7 of the first initial when jedi_done is set
esb_notes.B1:E59D: the three TIE pieces are types 9, 10 and 11 here, with timers $18, $18 and $10
esb_notes.B1:E683: in ESB this begins the explosion of a probot. BGBKN makes two pieces, not three: type 0 from a point $100 above the centre going left and type 2 (TMPTP3) from the centre going right, both with a random upward speed whose high byte TMPVZ is 0. both are drawn as object 6, the probot head
esb_notes.B1:E724: in ESB this begins the explosion of an AT-AT with piece types 6, 7 and 8, and it does not fall into BGBKN: its own three-piece code at $E72E, shared with atst_expl_setup, starts type TMPTP2 $200 ahead of the centre, TMPTP1 $200 to one side and TMPTP3 $200 to the other
esb_notes.B1:E846: 12 piece types in ESB: 0-2 probot, 3-5 AT-ST, 6-8 AT-AT, 9-11 TIE fighter
esb_notes.B1:E881: in ESB a piece that goes below ground level bounces: its height becomes half the depth it went below, and if it was falling its upward speed becomes half the falling speed. type 1's entry of TMV is expl_piece_kill instead
esb_notes.B1:E904: in ESB the type's view routine only picks the object and the colour (VWTIN), then obj_load, obj_points, obj_draw and obj_beam_home draw it: obj_points gives screen positions without a move to the object's centre first
esb_notes.B1:E99C: in ESB all 12 piece types come here. it does not call OBJCEN, the colour table has $18 entries and a timer of $18 or more gives a JSRL $A013

questions: B1:DA38-DAB2 - the .byte rows are code: six threaded draw primitives at $DA38, $DA3F, $DA5D, $DA7B, $DA9D and $DAA5 (given routine entries above). a search of both banks, the four slapstic pages and the vector ROM finds no word with any of these addresses, so the interpreter is unused and the lists it would have run are not in the ROM
B1:DAB3 - five bytes 10 6E 39 3C 00 between the threaded primitives and the text FULLER DID THE EFFECTS, not code that anything reaches and not referenced, purpose unknown
B1:E9E2-EA02 - 33 bytes after the explosion colour table that nothing refers to, purpose unknown

B1:DEFD - the carried name SDIV_B1 (self test divider) and its header sit in the middle of hs_view, dropped. the carried comments at $DEEE, $DEF3, $DEFD and $DF1B belonged to other Star Wars lines and are dropped too

B1:D9B3, D9B8, D9CB, D9D1 - the operands KFDEA and KFDEC are the numbers -534 and -532 (screen limits), not addresses in the ROM fill. B1:DF0C - LDD #$E1E1 is the address of the table at KE1E1. B1:E249 and E449 - the operand shown as cont_wave or HSCORS+40 is $4BEE as the end of the high score table
object 31 (draw_dart) - page 0 draws it twice in the tow cable code, each with its own roll angle. I could not tell from bank 1 what the two darts stand for
the table entries of objects 11 to 16 name draw_limb_down, but page 2 always draws limbs as objects 9 and 10, so those six entries are never used as draw routines
ram_notes and no_header are used here although the brief does not list them for this pass: ram_notes for COLOR ($48C0), which the game uses as the point buffer pointer, and no_header for $DEFD
